content.thinking:
I'm tracing the incident: deploy P2 at Oct 18 01:34 stripped out the month-total update logic from record_purchase, affecting both code paths and causing month totals to stop advancing from 01:36 onward, while readers continued pulling stale stored totals.

This surfaced as a silent data issue rather than an outage — shoppers' monthly statements (rendered via the stored total field) would have understated actual spend, with no visible errors or complaints logged in the record. I'm settling on framing the symptom as "shoppers' monthly spend totals fell behind their actual purchases" since that's the user-facing effect inferable from the code path, keeping it concise and number-free.

Tracing the cause: the stored month-total field wasn't being updated by either purchase-recording path in the currently running code, which traces back to deploy P2 of revision 26f1d7e, which removed the month-total update from one path (the other path never had it). I need to confirm this can't be pinned on the earlier P1 deploy instead — checking whether metrics show the service was healthy with P1 in place before the issue began, using the monitoring window anchored around the alert time.

Purchases before that 7-day window may not have been examined, so AL1's dating of the oldest affected purchase at A4 could be incomplete — but it seems the pattern still accepts AL1 as ruling out P1. Checking the diff, since purchase_ledger.py's month-total logic wasn't touched outside the shown hunk, that function stayed unchanged at the earlier commit too.

I'm also tracing whether a flag-gated path could have broken before P2, and whether AL1's 01:36 timestamp — just 1.5 minutes into the alert's lookback window — actually rules out P1 under the stated rule about alerts dating first harm after a later change.

AL1 dates the harm after P2, ruling out P1, and T14 rules out a flag-change cause since there were zero flag changes the hour before onset. The real mechanism: the change stopped updating the stored monthly total on the assumption it'd be derived on read, but the readers (U1-U3, U6) and reconciliation logic (U4/U5) still relied on the stale stored field, so it froze while actual purchases kept growing — though why the readers weren't updated alongside isn't shown.

This mechanism rests on the diff and source that actually ran (D1, S1) and the read paths (U rows), not on the unrun fallback path, so the hypothesis that it depends on code that never executed doesn't hold.

Contributing factors worth flagging: the reconciliation check only runs every few days so the drift went unnoticed, and the write path itself never flags discrepancies. Also, no test existed verifying the month total reconciles after record_purchase ran, so this gap wasn't caught before deploy — a CI check asserting reconciliation would have stopped it.

I'll propose adding a test that the stored month total reconciles after writes through record_purchase, run pre-deploy. Separately, the real root cause may be that readers of the stored field weren't updated alongside the writer, and the deploy itself came from a branch not merged into main's history, which is a distinct contributing factor worth noting.

I'll include it as a process item: nothing required the deployed revision to be on main. Also worth noting the alert paged nobody, so rollback had no one actively driving it sooner — this points to a detection/routing gap, like having this alert page on-call directly. For action items, the rollback to 4c810f2 should restore things alongside the existing AI-1 and AI-2.

I should also propose repairing the stored month totals for affected shoppers before the month rolls over (since the incident window closes right before Nov 1), run reconciliation checks more frequently than weekly as a detection fix, and route the alert to page on-call directly.

More importantly, I realize rollback doesn't fully resolve the issue — the derive-the-month path on the running branch is separately broken and wasn't touched by the diff, so if that feature flag is enabled for anyone, the bug persists even after rollback. Since flag state is unknown, I should flag this as still at risk and propose fixes: adding a deploy-pipeline test verifying month totals reconcile after writes, requiring deployed revisions to trace back through main's history, and separately addressing the broken derive path itself.

This mismatch keeps the spend summary and statements understated, and anything already recorded wrong stays wrong until it's repaired—ideally before the month rolls over, per F1's note.

For what went well, I'm noting Argus located the deployment and timed the diff review relative to the alert, and that Code-Fix proposed PR #344 with tests and a repair script after the alert—framing these as named actions without describing what the fix itself does.

For what went wrong: the Investigator split confidence across two candidate causes pointing at the same change (minor), but the real issue is that Code-Fix's draft was written against main rather than the deployed revision, so it doesn't actually touch the record_purchase change that ran in production—the branch it came from sits outside main entirely.

For got lucky: customers weren't financially harmed since the fault hit a reported figure rather than a charge, and the alert fired before the month rolled over, meaning a repair that recomputes from current-month purchases is still viable—had the check landed after rollover, the recomputed figure would have been wrong too.

Assumptions I'm relying on: the check only covers a limited window so I need to trust the dating for whether harm started earlier, and that readers on the main path match what's recorded as held. No shopper-reported symptoms exist, just inferred understated figures from the stored field, and error rate wasn't measured.

The plain-language cause: a code change stopped updating each shopper's running total when they made a purchase, while statements and checks kept reading the stale stored total, so it drifted behind actual purchases. I'm being careful to avoid writing specific numbers, keeping revision names and PR references as-is but using placeholder variables for timeframes.

For dating the issue, I'll reference when it started and the state of the fix rollout across replicas, then write it all up.

action_items.item: Repair the stored month totals that fell behind, before the month rolls over. One way is to review and then run the repair script proposed in PR #344 against an export of the accounts and load the result back.
Once the fix in PR #344 is merged, deploy a revision that carries it, so the derive_the_month path in what runs also updates the month total.
Run the month-total reconciliation far more often than every {A5} days, or check the stored total against purchases on write.
Add a test to the deploy pipeline that writes purchases through every recording path and asserts the stored month total reconciles with the current-month purchases.
Require any revision deployed to io-shop to be in main's history.
Route SpendTotalsDoNotReconcile to page the io-shop on-call.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers' stored month-spend totals no longer matched their purchases. The spend-integrity check found {A1} of {A2} shopper totals that did not reconcile with the purchases behind them. The widest was short by {A3}, and the oldest affected purchase was recorded at {A4}. Shopper-facing code reads that stored figure directly: the monthly statement (render_monthly_statement, _compared_with_usual, the_mean_purchase_this_month) and the spend summary (average_spend_per_item_this_month). So those figures came from a total that was too low.

The stored total_this_month_cents was not updated when a current-month purchase was recorded. In the code that ran, record_purchase updates only total_cents. record_purchase_deriving_the_month also updates only total_cents. So whichever path record_a_purchase took, the purchase was added and the month total stayed where it was. The reconciliation compares that field with the sum of this month's purchases and found it behind.

ruled_out.what: The earlier deploy P1 (revision 4c810f2). The alert dates the oldest affected purchase at {A4}, after P2 at {P2.1}, and under P1's revision record_purchase still updated the month total.
A flag change setting it off. The flag provider showed {T14.2} flag changes by anyone but Argus in the {T14.3} hour before the onset.

causal_chain.step: Deployment P2 at {P2.1} put revision 26f1d7e live, and that revision removed the month-total update from record_purchase. The diff against the previous revision shows the conditional addition to total_this_month_cents deleted, leaving only the total_cents addition. As of {T11.1}, all {T11.2} replicas were running this revision.

The change dropped the stored month total on the premise, stated in the new docstring, that the month figure "adds up from the history whenever anybody wants it". But the code that reads it was not changed to match. The statement, the spend summary and the reconciliation still read or divide by the stored total_this_month_cents instead of summing current-month purchases. So with the writer no longer updating the stored copy, every reader got a figure that fell further behind with each purchase.

input.cause_in_plain_words: A code change stopped the shop updating each shopper's stored spend total for the current month when they bought something, but the shop's statements and checks still read that stored total, so it fell behind what shoppers had actually bought.

contributing_factors.factor: The only check that compares stored month totals with purchases, the spend-integrity check, runs every {A5} days, and nothing in the write path notices a gap. The module's own docstring says nothing there notices when a total and the purchases disagree.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A check that ran far more often, or on write, would have flagged the gap soon after the deploy, not up to {A5} days later.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: Before the deploy, no test or check was seen that the stored month total still reconciles with the purchases after writes through record_purchase on the revision that was deployed.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A test like that would have failed on revision 26f1d7e and stopped the deploy.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

contributing_factors.factor: The revision that was deployed, 26f1d7e, is not in main's history, and nothing seen required a deployed revision to come from main.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The change would have had to pass whatever main's review and tests require before it ran, and a fix merged to main would reach what runs without a separate deploy from another branch.
contributing_factors.label: CF-3

contributing_factors.factor: The SpendTotalsDoNotReconcile alert paged nobody: no on-call incident was linked to it.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A person would have been told at once to roll back and repair the totals, instead of the action waiting as a recommendation.
contributing_factors.label: CF-4

got_lucky: The alert fired in the same month the totals went wrong. A repair that recomputes the month total from current-month purchases is still possible. Once the month rolls over, that recomputed figure would be wrong.
went_well: Argus placed the onset just after the deploy, {T6.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised, and read the suspect deployment's diff {T10.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised.
Argus checked the flag provider's history and found no flag change by anyone else before the onset, which narrowed the trigger to the deploy.
Code-Fix proposed a fix, new tests and a one-off repair script as draft PR #344, opened {T19.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised.
went_wrong: Code-Fix wrote its fix against main, which does not contain revision 26f1d7e, so the draft targets main's derive_the_month path and not the record_purchase change that actually ran.

input.root_cause: Revision 26f1d7e removed the update of the stored per-shopper month total (total_this_month_cents) from record_purchase, assuming the month figure would be worked out from purchase history whenever it was needed. But the monthly statement, the spend summary and the reconciliation still read the stored field. The other write path, record_purchase_deriving_the_month, also leaves the field unchanged. So every current-month purchase written since then left the stored month total further below the purchases behind it.
input.still_at_risk: The running revision still leaves the stored month total unchanged on every current-month purchase, so the totals already written wrong stay wrong and keep falling further behind until somebody repairs them, and the repair has to happen before the month rolls over; also, the flag-selected path that derives the month (derive_the_month) leaves the total unchanged both in the revision that ran and in the one before it, so rolling back alone does not cover shoppers on that path.
input.symptom: Shoppers' stored spend totals for this month fell behind the purchases they had made
